common.sessionExpired: Your session expired — reload the page and try again.

firewall.title: Firewall Rules
firewall.subtitle: Allow or block ports and addresses. A change you do not keep within the time shown is undone.
firewall.loadFailed: Unable to load the firewall rules.
firewall.addFailed: The rule could not be added.
firewall.removeFailed: The rule could not be removed.
firewall.confirmFailed: The change could not be kept.
firewall.undone: The change was not kept in time, so it has been undone.
firewall.formHelp: Give a port, a source address, or both. A block is checked before every allow.
firewall.empty: No rules added from dPanel yet.
firewall.onlyOurs: Only rules in the shapes dPanel writes are listed. Rules written by hand on the server are left alone.
firewall.pendingHelp: Click Keep within {seconds} seconds, or the firewall goes back to how it was. If this page stops answering, the change locked you out and will be undone.

siteLogs.title: Logs
siteLogs.subtitle: Requests to {domain} and its PHP errors.
siteLogs.accessHelp: Each line: client, time, request, status, bytes, referrer, browser and milliseconds taken. The log rotates at 10 MB and keeps five old files.
siteLogs.phpHelp: PHP errors of every site this account owns. Sites made before this log existed keep logging where they did until their PHP pool is made again.
siteLogs.noWafLog: The firewall has not matched any request yet.
siteLogs.wafHelp: Requests the web application firewall matched: time, client, request, what it did (blocked, would-block or matched), the status it chose, and the rules. Only requests to PHP or an app are checked.

wordpress.title: WordPress
wordpress.subtitle: Every WordPress site you manage: updates, staging copies and a security check.
wordpress.none: No WordPress site was found among your websites.
wordpress.bulkConfirm: Update {count} sites now? Each site is updated in turn.
wordpress.updateHelp: Updates run with plugins and themes switched off for the command, so a broken plugin cannot stop its own update. Take a staging copy first for a big update.
wordpress.securityHelp: Checks core files against wordpress.org, plugin files, admin names, open registration, debug mode and file editing.
wordpress.fixFailed: The fix could not be applied.
wordpress.reinstallConfirm: Download WordPress core again over the current files? Content, plugins and themes are not touched.

core_files.issue: Some core files are changed or should not be there

admin_names.pass: No administrator has an easily guessed name
admin_names.issue: An administrator has an easily guessed name

debug.issue: Debug mode is on and can show errors to visitors

file_edit.pass: The theme and plugin file editor is off
file_edit.issue: Admins can edit PHP files from wp-admin

plugin_updates.pass: All plugins are up to date

wordpress.stagingHelp: Pair this site with another of your sites as its staging copy. Copying replaces the other site's files and database (they go to the trash first) and rewrites the site address.
wordpress.noFreeSite: Create another website to use as staging first
wordpress.unlinkConfirm: Unpair these sites? Neither site is changed.
wordpress.copyConfirm: Copy {from} over {to}? {to}'s current files and database go to the trash first.
wordpress.deployConfirm: Deploy {from} over the live site {to}? The live files and database go to the trash first.

stage.testing: Updating and testing the staging copy…

wordpress.safeHelp: Copy this site over its staging site, update the copy, and update this site only if the copy still loads without errors. Needs a linked staging site.
wordpress.safeStarted: Safe update started. Follow it on the Staging tab.

mailForwarders.title: Forwarders & Catch-all
mailForwarders.subtitle: Addresses that only forward, and where mail to unknown addresses goes
mailForwarders.formHelp: No mailbox is made: mail to this address goes straight on. Separate several addresses with commas.
mailForwarders.removeConfirm: Stop forwarding {address}? Mail to it will be refused.
mailForwarders.catchAllHelp: Mail to an address of the domain that has no mailbox or forwarder goes here. Leave empty to refuse it.
mailForwarders.noDomains: You have no website or mailbox domain yet.

smtpRelay.title: SMTP Relay
smtpRelay.subtitle: Send all outgoing mail through another server
smtpRelay.help: TLS is always required. The password goes to Postfix and is not stored by the panel, so enter it again whenever you save.
smtpRelay.disableConfirm: Send outgoing mail directly from this server again?

autoresponder.title: Automatic reply
autoresponder.help: Answers each sender once per interval, never to spam or mailing lists.
autoresponder.subject: Subject
autoresponder.interval: Days between replies to one sender
autoresponder.loadFailed: The automatic reply could not be loaded.
autoresponder.saveFailed: The automatic reply was not saved.

branding.title: Branding
branding.serverHelp: The name, logo and colour everyone sees, unless their reseller has their own.
branding.resellerHelp: The name, logo and colour you and your customers see.
branding.name: Panel name
branding.logoHelp: PNG, JPG or WebP, at most 512 KB.
branding.fallback: Anything left empty comes from the server's branding, then dPanel's own.

customCertificate.title: Upload a certificate for {domain}
customCertificate.help: Use a certificate you bought or were given. It is checked before it is installed: it must be for this domain, not expired, and match the key.
customCertificate.note: It is not renewed automatically: you get a notification 30, 7 and 1 days before it expires. To go back to a free certificate, use Reinstall SSL.
customCertificate.fileTooLarge: That file is too large to be a certificate or a key.

dnssec.title: DNSSEC
dnssec.on: This zone is signed. Add the DS record below at your domain registrar; until then, resolvers treat the zone as unsigned.
dnssec.off: Signing lets resolvers check that answers for this domain really come from this server.
dnssec.registrar: DS records for your registrar (most want the one with digest type 2):
dnssec.confirmEnable: Sign this zone? Nothing changes for visitors until you add the DS record at your registrar.
dnssec.confirmDisable: Remove the DS record at your registrar first and wait a day. If it is still there when signing stops, the domain stops resolving. Turn off DNSSEC now?

wildcardSsl.help: One certificate for {domain} and every *.{domain} subdomain. The domain's DNS must be on this server or on Cloudflare.
wildcardSsl.confirmOn: Issue a wildcard certificate for {domain} and *.{domain}? A TXT record is added to the domain's DNS while the CA checks it. This can take a few minutes.
wildcardSsl.confirmOff: Stop covering *.{domain}? {domain} gets a plain certificate, and subdomains without their own certificate lose HTTPS.

dnsTransfers.title: Zone Transfers
dnsTransfers.subtitle: Secondary nameservers that copy this server's DNS zones
dnsTransfers.secondariesHelp: Each server listed here may copy (AXFR) all {count} zones this server is primary for, and is sent a NOTIFY whenever one changes.
dnsTransfers.none: No secondaries. Only this server answers for its zones.
dnsTransfers.label: Name (optional)
dnsTransfers.removeConfirm: Stop {address} from copying zones from this server?
dnsTransfers.step1: Add each zone there as a secondary zone with this server's IP as its primary. On another dPanel server: DNS Zones → Add domains, type slave.
dnsTransfers.step2: Give the secondary a nameserver name and list it with this server's ({nameservers}) in DNS_OUR_NAMESERVERS, so every zone carries its NS record.
dnsTransfers.step3: Add the secondary's name at each domain's registrar, next to this server's.
dnsTransfers.copiedHelp: Secondary zones: PowerDNS copies them from their primary and keeps them up to date. Their records are changed on the primary.
dnsTransfers.noCopied: None. Add one under DNS Zones with the type slave.

incrementalBackups.title: Incremental backups
incrementalBackups.subtitle: Encrypted restore points: each backup stores only what changed
incrementalBackups.keyHelp: Every restore point is encrypted with this key. Without it nobody can read the backups, not you and not us, and a lost server takes the key with it. Download it and keep it somewhere other than this server.
incrementalBackups.keySaved: I have saved the key somewhere else
incrementalBackups.notConfigured: Not set up yet. Choose where the restore points go.
incrementalBackups.notConfiguredUser: Incremental backups are not set up on this server yet.
incrementalBackups.existingPasswordHelp: Leave empty to create a new repository with a new key.

kindHelp.local: Safe from mistakes, not from losing the disk. Prefer storage on another machine.
kindHelp.sftp: drust logs in with root's SSH key; add it to the backup server first.
kindHelp.s3: The keys are stored encrypted and only given to restic.
kindHelp.rclone: Set up the remote first with rclone config as root.

incrementalBackups.restorePointsHelp: Each one holds the website's files and databases as they were at that moment.

incrementalRestore.title: Restore
incrementalRestore.subtitle: Restore point of {when} ({id})
incrementalRestore.filesHelp: What you pick comes back in a new restored-… folder in the website's home. Nothing there now is changed; move what you need.
incrementalRestore.empty: This folder is empty in the restore point.
incrementalRestore.browseFailed: The restore point could not be read.
incrementalRestore.databasesHelp: The database goes back to how it was. What it holds now is saved first, as a .sql file in the restored-… folder.
incrementalRestore.mailboxesHelp: The messages come back in a new mail folder, Restored-…, next to what is in the mailbox now. Subscribe to it in the mail program if it does not show.
incrementalRestore.confirmFiles: Restore {path} into a new restored-… folder?
incrementalRestore.confirmDatabase: Put {name} back as it was? Its current content is saved first.
incrementalRestore.confirmMailbox: Bring back the messages of {email} into a new Restored-… folder?

restoreTest.title: Restore test
restoreTest.help: A backup only counts if it comes back. Each week, after that day's scheduled backup, restic checks the repository and reads back part of the stored data, then every website's newest restore point is read as a restore would read it: each database dump in full, which must end like a finished dump, and a spread of the home's files, which must match their recorded size. Nothing is written to the websites.
restoreTest.overdue: No restore test has passed since {when}.
restoreTest.neverPassed: No restore test has passed yet.
restoreTest.weekly: Test the restore points every week
restoreTest.settingsHelp: The test runs right after the scheduled backup on that day, so it never competes with it. Reading more data finds more damage but takes longer, and costs download fees on cloud storage.
restoreTest.needsSchedule: The daily backup is off, so the weekly test does not run. Turn the schedule on, or use Test now.
restoreTest.noRuns: No restore test has run yet.
restoreTest.repositoryCheck: Repository check, {percent}% of the data read back

apiTokens.title: API Tokens
apiTokens.subtitle: Tokens let your own scripts and tools use the dPanel API. A token can only do what you can do in the panel.
apiTokens.limits: Each token may make 120 requests a minute. Requests stop working while your account is suspended.
apiTokens.name: Name
apiTokens.noScopes: Your account may not use any part of the API.
apiTokens.scopeHelp: Give a token only what it needs. Changes made with a token are written to the activity log.
apiTokens.createFailed: The token could not be created.
apiTokens.shownOnce: Copy this token now. It is not shown again.
apiTokens.revokeConfirm: Revoke "{name}"? Anything using it stops working at once.
apiTokens.revokeFailed: The token could not be revoked.

panelUpdate.title: Updates
panelUpdate.help: Update dPanel to a newer release, or roll an update back.
panelUpdate.updateHelp: The panel backs up its .env, database and code first. If the new version fails to install or its checks fail, the backup is restored on its own. The panel may not answer for a few minutes while it restarts.
panelUpdate.confirmUpdate: Update dPanel to {ref} now? The panel restarts during the update.
panelUpdate.alreadyRunning: An update is running. Open its log in the history below.
panelUpdate.noCommitList: GitHub could not list the changes for this version.
panelUpdate.reconnecting: Waiting for the panel to answer again; it restarts during the update.
panelUpdate.noHistory: No update has run from the panel yet.
panelUpdate.rollbackHelp: The code and .env from before this update are put back, then the update steps run again on them. A backup of the current state is taken first.
panelUpdate.restoreDatabaseHelp: Taken at {time}. Everything changed in the panel since then is lost: websites, mailboxes, DNS records and users.
panelUpdate.keepDatabaseWarning: The database stays as it is. If the newer version changed its tables, the older code may not work with them.
